title: Pan Am 812
summary: Pan Am Flight 812, a Boeing 707, crashed into a mountain near Denpasar, Bali on April 22, 1974 while preparing for approach to Ngurah Rai Airport. Multiple eyewitnesses reported the aircraft was on fire before striking Mesehe Mountain, and the crew appears to have attempted approach from the northwest where terrain was steeper rather than the standard eastern approach.
probable_cause: The aircraft struck a mountain during approach to Denpasar. Investigation concluded the aircraft did not break up in flight, engines were functioning properly, and the aircraft was airworthy. The crew's attempt to approach from the northwest into mountainous terrain was the primary factor.

factors.evidence: Captain Zinke was trying to land from the northwest, where the mountains were located, rather than the usual route from the east
the aircraft descended below the MSL elevation of Mesehe Mountain without terrain clearance
the pilot-in-command requested the visibility by calling but this message was never received by the Bali Tower
it was subsequently found that the aircraft had hit a mountain approximately 37 mi northwest of the Bali airport

events.text: First contact between aircraft and Bali Tower at 15:06 UTC
Flight 812 reported reaching 2,500 feet and requested visibility information
Pilot requested tower visibility information; this message was never received by Bali Tower
Crew descended toward Mesehe Mountain from northwest rather than standard eastern approach
Aircraft struck Mesehe Mountain; tower attempting contact received no response

notes: Investigation hampered by Indonesian Government decision to stop investigation
Multiple eyewitnesses reported fire before impact
Aircraft broke up only on impact, not in flight
Specific cause of crew's navigation decision not documented

title: Martinair 138
summary: A Douglas DC-8 operating a hajj charter flight from Surabaya to Jeddah via Colombo encountered deteriorating weather on approach. The crew descended to 2000 ft and continued descent without sighting the airport, striking the Saptha Kanya mountain range at 4355 ft approximately 40 nautical miles east of Colombo, killing all 191 occupants.
probable_cause: Controlled flight into terrain resulting from descent below safe altitude due to crew misidentification of position relative to airport, relying on onboard Doppler and Weather Radar systems.

factors.evidence: Crew misidentified their position vis-a-vis the airport based on Doppler and Weather Radar systems.
Crew continued descent below minimum altitude without sighting the airport or visual contact.
Colombo area experiencing poor visibility and deteriorating weather on approach.
Aircraft crashed into Saptha Kanya mountain range at 4355 ft approximately 40 nautical miles east of Colombo.

events.text: Aircraft contacted Katunayaka approach at 130 miles out; approach control reported weather and requested crew change to Colombo area control.
Aircraft descended from 35000 ft and was cleared to 2000 ft by approach control, required to report if airport in sight.
Crew did not sight airport and made no further radio contact; aircraft flying at abnormally low level.
Aircraft struck the fifth mountain of Saptha Kanya mountain range at 4355 ft approximately 40 nautical miles east of Colombo with all 191 on board killed.

notes: 182 of 191 occupants were Indonesian Hajj pilgrims
deadliest in Sri Lankan aviation history
